steps.say: The past progressive shows an action that was going on in the past. Use was or were with an -ing verb.
steps.show: I was reading. They were playing.

steps.say: It is often used when another action interrupts it.
steps.show: I was reading when the phone rang.

steps.say: The present perfect uses has or have with a past form. It links the past to now.
Some verbs have a special form after has or have.
steps.show: go → gone, eat → eaten, see → seen, write → written

steps.say: Use has with he, she or it. Use have with I, you, we and they.
steps.show: She has eaten. We have eaten.

steps.say: Do not use the present perfect with a finished time like yesterday.
steps.show: I saw it yesterday. I have seen it.

check.prompt: We ___ swimming when the whistle blew.

options.why: Was goes with I, he, she or it. We needs a different word.
Blew is in the past, so we need a past form.
Have is not used with swimming like this.

hints: Blew tells you this is in the past.
The swimming was going on when the whistle blew.
Was or were: which goes with we?
check.explanation: With we in the past progressive, we use were: we were swimming.

check.prompt:
Write has or have.
Ana ___ finished her drawing.
hints: Which helper word goes with she?
check.explanation: Ana is one person, like she, so we use has: Ana has finished her drawing.
